page: Amazon Web Services r5.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processors operating at 3.1 GHz, featuring 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via two threads per core. The hardware implementation includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache, alongside core execution flags such as AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, and bit manipulation primitives. System memory totals 512.0 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle dedicated GPUs and contains no local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes over a 20 Gbps baseline network link.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong sustained memory throughput alongside middle-tier multi-threaded processing. The large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 216.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieved 95.17 GB/sec, placing the instance in the top 25 percent for high-volume memory transfers. The aggregate multi-threaded compute performance settled firmly within the middle tier, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 55,060.5 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 11,288.0. In database testing, the instance managed 21,283.69 Passmark database operations and 50.64 million Redis SET operations per second, supported by static web throughput of 35.73 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the r5.16xlarge lies in single-threaded processing and specialized serial tasks. Single-core performance sits in the lower quartile, as illustrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,019.0, single-threaded gzip throughput of 21.69 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 8.21 GB/sec. Serial LLM text generation is similarly constrained, measuring 42.21 tokens per second on a small 135M parameter model and 7.52 tokens per second on a 7B model. Consequently, cost efficiency favors highly parallelized, memory-dense enterprise services over single-threaded or serial computational workloads.

The r5.16xlarge fits large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data processing frameworks, enterprise-tier web serving pools, and batch ETL workflows requiring substantial RAM allocations.
